# On android a window's `@key` is a hardware keyboard's key, heard before
# anything in the window hears it: SnglWindowKeys sits in front of the
# activity's window callback, which the decor view hands a key to before any
# view. A test's key is heard as the test gives it, and one the handler leaves
# is pressed into the decor view as the system would, where the focused field
# types it, the focused button presses on its Enter and Tab moves the focus;
# one it stops goes nowhere, and the test's stop is told. Before, the window
# heard only the keys nothing focused took, and only by name.

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin keys.sngl
stdout 'ok   5 tests, 0 failures'

-- keys.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component app root {
    var heard = ""
    var text = ""
    var pressed = 0
    var stopping = false

    ui.window #main(title="Keys", @key(e, stop) {
        var mods = ""
        if e.ctrl {
            mods = mods + "ctrl+"
        }
        if e.editing {
            mods = mods + "editing+"
        }
        heard = heard + "[" + mods + e.key + "]"
        if !stopping {
            return
        }
        stop()
    }) {
        ui.vbox {
            ui.input #shown(value="shown", readonly=true)
            ui.button #go(text="go", @click { pressed += 1 })
            ui.input #field(:value=text)
            ui.text(value=heard)
        }
    }
}

app()

func testAKeyIsHeardAndGoesOn(t test.Test, c app) {
    var stopped = false
    c.field.focus()
    c.main.key(ui.KeyPress{key="h", editing=true}, func() { stopped = true })
    c.main.key(ui.KeyPress{key="i", editing=true}, func() { stopped = true })
    t.assert(c.heard == "[editing+h][editing+i]")
    t.assert(c.text == "hi")
    t.assert(!stopped)
}

func testAStoppedKeyTypesNothing(t test.Test, c app) {
    var stopped = 0
    c.field.focus()
    c.stopping = true
    c.main.key(ui.KeyPress{key="h", editing=true}, func() { stopped += 1 })
    c.main.key(ui.KeyPress{key="s", ctrl=true, editing=true}, func() { stopped += 1 })
    t.assert(c.heard == "[editing+h][ctrl+editing+s]")
    t.assert(c.text == "")
    t.assert(stopped == 2)
}

func testEnterGoesOnToTheFocusedButton(t test.Test, c app) {
    c.shown.focus()
    c.main.key(ui.KeyPress{key="Tab"}, func() {})
    c.main.key(ui.KeyPress{key="Enter"}, func() {})
    t.assert(c.heard == "[Tab][Enter]")
    t.assert(c.pressed == 1)
}

func testAStoppedEnterPressesNothing(t test.Test, c app) {
    c.shown.focus()
    c.main.key(ui.KeyPress{key="Tab"}, func() {})
    c.stopping = true
    c.main.key(ui.KeyPress{key="Enter"}, func() {})
    t.assert(c.pressed == 0)
}

func testAStoppedTabMovesNoFocus(t test.Test, c app) {
    c.field.focus()
    c.stopping = true
    c.main.key(ui.KeyPress{key="Tab", editing=true}, func() {})
    c.stopping = false
    c.main.key(ui.KeyPress{key="a", editing=true}, func() {})
    t.assert(c.text == "a")
    t.assert(c.heard == "[editing+Tab][editing+a]")
}
